utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, the accused, in his cross-examination, is entitled to put you a leading question. However, you are free to answer in the manner you like to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We will set that subject aside. Let me ask you, because Mr. Tieger confirmed today on your behalf that Bratunac was peaceful and quiet and there were no problems until Serbs suddenly went on a rampage, is it the case that in July 1991, Muslim extremists were burning Serbian flags and went -- used them as a toilet?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: You mean 1991?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Just answer whatever you think is right.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't think so. I would have known. It would have been discussed at all sorts of meetings if it had happened. Public debates would have been organised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it true that in end August, a representative of the JNA came to remove the files of military conscripts? He was refused, and then in mid-August a unit came to do the same, however, the Muslims gathered in front of the municipal building and prevented him from -- prevented the JNA from taking those files?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: First of all, SDS President Deronjic came to the national defence secretariat together with other representatives of the party asking for those files. Of course, the national defence secretary had no authority. He was not authorised to turn over such important documentation to the SDS. They threatened him. They said they would throw him out of the window. He called the police, and the police put guards at his office. Later on SDS activists organised a rally. They gathered a lot of people --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Wait. Wait. We'll come to that. Let's take things in sequence. First of all, one or two representatives of the JNA came. Are you trying to say it was not a representative of the JNA, that it was Deronjic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: We have to place things in their own time-frame. I am talking about the day when a unit of the JNA came to remove that documentation. I think you are talking about the day before when one of JNA officers came to ask for the documentation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: A few days before a JNA representative came to take what belonged rightfully to the Federal Secretariat for National Defence. All military documentation belonged to the national Secretariat for Defence.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know if anybody came a few days earlier to ask for that documentation. Let's assume that that's right. The Secretary for National Defence reports to the command in Tuzla and nobody from that command in Tuzla came to ask him for that documentation, and he was not authorised to turn it over to somebody from outside, from -- from another land.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You mean to say this JNA representative did not come from the corps in Tuzla?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: No, he didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: That Secretary for National Defence, was he also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And the commander of the Territorial Defence was also a Muslim?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is it true that not long after that the SDS flag was burnt again and Serbs in Kravica were told and threatened that their houses would be burnt down, and in a display of power, people were driving by their houses with rifles protruding from the windows?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Especially that last thing is not true. It's impossible that Muslims would have driven by Serb houses displaying their long barrels, absolute impossible.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I would say it's a purposely misleading question to say, "Is it true that not long after that the SDS flag was burned again ...," when the witness failed to confirm that proposition when put to him by Dr. Karadzic. So Dr. Karadzic was trying to get it in the back door by building it into a question and hoping it will somehow pass unnoticed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: However, it was answered, fortunately. Let us move on, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Did a major crisis break out in mid-September when heads rolled?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: When SDS activists set up an ambush in a hamlet near Kravica and shot at a car with four Bosniaks in it, wounding two, of course that started a crisis, tensions spread anxiety among people.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's deal with the set of different subjects. I would like to call up 1D3876. Mr. Gusic, this is the command of the 17th Corps, the security section, based in Tuzla. That is December 1991. It says cross-section of paramilitary organisations in the area of responsibility of the 7th Corps to the south of the Sava River. That corps had a zone of responsibility that stretched into Croatia. Do you see the heading?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could we look at page 3 -- or, rather, let's not, not to waste time. Let's look at page 4. In fact, let's look at page 3 and then 4 to see that they are observing Serbs and Muslims and Croats alike and making notes. Concerning the area of Derventa, most of the paramilitary units are those of the HDZ. Can we see page 4. This says that the SDA -- in fact, they don't have information about the SDA in Derventa, but in Dubocac, the HDZ is distributing weapons, and about the Serbs they enumerate what is being set up and who is being armed. So quite impartially they are keeping tabs on all the three parties. Let's look at page 16 in Serbian. We'll see your municipality there. Please look at this: Paramilitary units of the SDA in the municipality of Zvornik namely in Drinjaca, Sapna, Grabovica, Kamenica and Kozluk, and in Zvornik itself, smaller units up to company strong have been set up in Bratunac, including Glogova, Konjevic Polje, and Repovac. Volunteer SDA units were set up. And then it says according to a plan from the head office of the SDA in Sarajevo, it is envisaged that the military Crisis Staff for --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It's very difficult to find where you are reading from.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Territory Zvornik, Bratunac, and Srebrenica. [In English] It must be probably in English -- in Serbian 16th page, but in English probably 16th or 17th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The English has only five pages.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Oh. That means that not the whole document has been translated. Let's skip Brcko and look for Zvornik, Bratunac and Srebrenica on the next page. Only segments of this have been translated it seems. Can we find in English the sub-heading Zvornik, Bratunac, and Srebrenica. [In English] Could you list please English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It has only two pages of text and three pages of diagrams, and I can't find that passage.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can you see that there is a reference to battalions, 500 in each municipality? The target levels have not been reached, so work needs to be speeded up. SDA-organised units will become part of larger units and will become part of a brigade and that brigade will become part of the division together with the brigade from Foca, Gorazde.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: This needs to be reviewed carefully. You can't just interpret it the way you are doing. This document is dated 30th December 1991. That's just three or four months before the aggression against Bosnia and Herzegovina and the occupation of our municipalities. The Serbs were armed to their teeth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll come to that.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: And the JNA was so overwhelmingly strong. I think this document looks to me like something the -- the army made up to justify some of their actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You will see that they are not sparing the Serbs either. I'm asking you, do you see that the army made an assessment and found out that the SDA head office intends every municipality to have a 500-strong battalion, and they will all be united in a division called the Drina Division. And under number 4 we can see that every municipality formed an illegal Muslim police force consisting of 30 men and the corps personnel are demobilised members of the police stations.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: We need to deal with this with some precision. Look at number 2. The territory of Bratunac and Srebrenica, where it says in the villages Glogova, Konjevic Polje, and Repovac, volunteer SDA units have been set up. I can guarantee that not a single SDA volunteer unit had been established.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let us see what they say about the Serbs, the SDS, in the villages of Podgradac, Kravica, Kajici, Mali Borici, Bljeceva, Greca [phoen], is it, Grabovacka Rijeka, and Polum [phoen] in Bratunac, armed volunteer units were established consisting of locals who have a pro-Chetnik orientation. Can we move on to the next page, 18. Number 2 says Skelani, Lijesce, Podravanje, pro-Chetnik volunteer units were established. Do you know, Mr. Witness, that all Serb units resubordinate themselves to the JNA and volunteered and that the JNA objected to their ideological orientation and that those were the only volunteer units from the Serb side?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about that. I can talk about Bratunac, and I can speak with full responsibility and in a qualified manner, as one would say. They established a Crisis Staff for Bratunac and all the settlements there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that. Have you heard of Nurif Rizvanovic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Number 8, this is what the JNA says about him: Nurif Rizvanovic a former junior officer tried as a B and D agent, that's the German Secret Service, now involved in the arming and establishment of armed formations of the SDA in the territory of Bratunac and Srebrenica. Do you know that he was supposed to be commander of the Drina Division.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: As for this Nurif Rizvanovic, I know of him, that he was a former JNA officer, that he ended his professional career in the JNA. Nurif is from Glogova. He was born in Glogova. This is a village in the municipality of Bratunac. Five or 6 kilometres away from the centre of Bratunac. He would usually come to that village in 1991. I think it was the summer of 1991. When he came to his village of Glogova, he came with some information to the effect that the JNA, and he was an officer of that army and he did have that kind of knowledge, well, that the JNA and Serbia are planning to carve out a Greater Serbia at the expense of Bosnia and that the Bosniaks have to be prepared for that unless they intend to see this done at their expense. He also tried to establish some council. I think it was called the Muslim council. He got a few people together, I think, in the village of Glogova and perhaps two or three other local communes. I don't think he had more than 15 or 20 persons who were like-minded. At that time, I think the Belgrade media wrote that he was a triple agent, that he collaborated with the KOS and that he worked for the German intelligence service as well as the Italian intelligence service. So the Muslims of Bratunac, when they found out about this, they didn't believe it. These attempts fell through. And the legal organs of the Municipality of Bratunac banned these activities of his and I believe he had to leave in the beginning of September of 1991 because of that. That is what I have to say about Nurif Rizvanovic in that period of time, that is, that we are discussing now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it not correct that Nurif Rizvanovic commanded units that were linked to Konjevic Polje, Cerska in this area between Zvornik, Vlasenica, and Bratunac and that he was liquidated by Naser Oric who declared him a traitor?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I am going to answer that question for you. I know about that, I know something about it. I mean it may be useful to this Court. I remembered just now and you will remember better than me whether this is true or not. Rizvanovic came to our office. I happened to be there and he called this person from the SDA and he said, "come with me." "Where are you going?" "I'm going to Sarajevo. I have a meeting with Radovan Karadzic and Fikret Abdic." So he seemed rather convincing. I had the impression that he really knew you and Abdic and many other important people in Sarajevo. You probably know quite a bit about him. I do too. There are things that I want to say here. When Bratunac was occupied, when over 20.000 Muslims from Bratunac were exterminated from Bratunac, when almost 1.000 civilians were killed and when all of these camps were organised, this was exceptionally cruel torture, and these victims were later exchanged. After two or three months when all these Bosniaks were expelled, many of them were staying in Zivinice, Lukavac, Srebrenik, Tuzla, and so on, Nurif Rizvanovic appeared wanting to organise these people who had been expelled and to return to the municipality of Srebrenica in that way. He managed to bring together about 400 volunteers who were, indeed, motivated at the time in view of everything they had experienced. They wanted to go back to that area. He managed to arm them to a maximum, and he managed to get through the lines, fortified lines from Kalesija to the encircled area of Bratunac -- or, rather, Konjevic Polje, Bratunac, Srebrenica. So these 400 armed men, he managed to get them into that encircled area and to continue the fighting that you've been talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. MTS is military equipment; right? So that the interpreters would know what you mean.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we have the last page of this document. Do you see that diagram for Bosnia, the political staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina on the left-hand side and on the right-hand side, the military staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina. In the middle it says the Crisis Staff of the north-east -- of north-eastern Bosnia. This is the diagram that had been completed in 1991, Mr. Gusic. Is it possible that you, as a prominent member of the SDA, and later on an officer of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina were excluded from these preparations?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, the right person to talk to in respect of this diagram is someone who stands behind it, and you probably know who that is, and I'm not going to go into that now. As for my inclusion or exclusion, I can only talk about the municipality of Bratunac. As for the municipality of Bratunac, I said during the introductory questions put to me by the distinguished Prosecutor, I explained some things, namely what the situation was when I became president of the municipality, that the Serb people were armed and that Serb civilians were being trained how to use these weapons, trained by the JNA, the SDS, et cetera. At the time, I wanted to see how prepared the Muslim people were, whether they could do anything to defend themselves if there were to be incursions or an occupation of Bratunac. Before I came to this position at the level of the municipality of Bratunac we had some discussions within the SDA, since we had that information. People were saying something should be organised. Something should be done. We have to defend ourselves. We should not just go with the tide. This should be an advantage of ours. Now, was it the month of February or January? I don't know. I'm not sure. The Municipal Board of the SDA adopted a conclusion or decision to establish -- now, was it a Crisis Staff? I think we called it a staff for the defence of Bratunac. And also a person was appointed commander of that staff. All of that was on paper basically. This person was charged with touring the entire area, finding capable people in each and every village who could form units in their respective villages, and then if there were to be an attack, they should be able to defend themselves. I think that in the beginning some persons were appointed, but about 10 days before Bratunac was occupied, all of these activists, or most of them, realised that there was this danger lurking, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Please, let me finish. So all of them left, literally all of them, including the one who was in charge of heading that staff. So on the 17th of April, 1992, Bratunac had all of these foreign military units from Serbia enter the area without putting up any resistance whatsoever. Not a single bullet was fired.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this document be admitted and then we're going to call up another one and then you're going to see that that was not the case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I've been trying to monitor the extent to which this document was or was not illuminated by the information that the witness had and the extent to which it's being -- it was proffered for the purpose of allegedly impeaching something the witness said. It was actually quite confusing to me, and it -- that confusion was magnified by the fact that I couldn't view the document because it's not translated. So I -- I think the thrust of it is such that it would not normally be one that would I object to, but I'm -- by virtue of the way in which it was used and the problems associated with the lack of translation, which, by the way, which was fairly apparent given the disparity between the size of the actual document and the translation itself, I'm just going to leave it in the Chamber's hands. I don't want to make too much of a fuss about it, but it was problematic. Maybe Mr. Robinson can illuminate more about the underlying purpose of tendering the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I wonder the witness has confirmed anything about this document. Mr. Robinson, can you help us as to the relevance of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm going to defer to Dr. Karadzic on that point. My only observation would be that enough of discussion about the document would help the Chamber if the document was admitted for the context but, in terms of its actual relevance, I'll leave that to Dr. Karadzic. He's better placed to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Excellency. This is a document of the JNA that has equidistance, ideological and any other kind, in view of all the parties in Bosnia, and they are quite impartially registering everyone's conduct, that is to say the conduct of all three parties in Bosnia, all three peoples in Bosnia, and the rise in tensions. It is being said here that only the Serbs were organised, and you can see here that everyone is organised, whereas the Serbs consider themselves to be volunteers and they place themselves under the command of the JNA, whereas the Muslims and the Croats have their own commands. I think this is relevant, because, inter alia, this has to do with all of north-eastern Bosnia, including Bratunac and its villages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, that actually didn't quite take the form of the document's relationship to the manner in which it was used with the witness. I will say it seemed to be in the nature of almost a bar table submission. If it were a bar table submission, the Prosecution would be in a position to identify other documentation and evidence contradicting the proposition the JNA was equidistant and ideologically neutral, and that's -- I was going to say, this is another example of something I mentioned earlier that when we are not in a position to, particularly not in a position to respond by way of redirect because we don't have the translation of the document where we should -- the Prosecution or the other party if the situation is reversed should be permitted latitude to proffer bar table documents to deal with issues presented by the document which we determine when it's ultimately translated.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The witness has not confirmed anything about this document, and the Chamber doesn't find it necessary or relevant to understand the context of the witness's evidence, so we'll not admit this. And we'll have a break for 25 minutes, and resume at five to 6.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. May I ask the legal officer to put a document on the ELMO -- the usher, rather, and I hope the Prosecution will tell us its provenance, because it's one page from a book they disclosed to us, ERN 01389586. That's right, the page with the number. That's the one we need now. We don't have time for the rest. [In English] This page that is under the number.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, I have to read out to you. I have to read because it's not been translated because I didn't know you would challenge these things. The SDA branch in Bratunac sent its delegation to the founding meeting of the Patriotic League of the region of Tuzla on the 11th January 1992, to Tojsici, Kalesija municipality, and the members of the delegation were as follows: Nijaz Dubicic, president of the municipality and Sabit Mujkic, commander of the Territorial Defence of Bratunac. At the meeting in Tojsici, at the request of the Bratunac delegation, a decision was made to send to Bratunac Samir Nistovic to coordinate the work of the Patriotic League of Bratunac and help with the drafting of defence plans for the municipality of Bratunac. The Bratunac delegation proposed that Nedzib Husic from Bratunac be appointed commander of the Patriotic League for the subregion (Bratunac, Zvornik, and Vlasenica) whose rank was major in the Territorial Defence of Bratunac and the proposal was accepted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: First, what is this about? You have to tell what book this is, and second, what's the relevance of these questions?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Excellency, if I may draw your attention to the middle of the page where you see the name of this witness, Dzevad Gusic. It's approximately line 20. Dzevad Gusic and all the other participants in these preparations and it says that the SDA of Bratunac formed the Patriotic League in 1991 or, rather, planned to, and put these plans into practice in 1992. This contradicts directly what the witness is saying. Secondly, it points to his involvement. And third, if I'm not allowed to challenge the credibility and the allegations of this witness then this is a waste of time. The Prosecution provided this document, but only one page of it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: The only thing I wanted to -- to mention, Mr. President, was that Mr. Karadzic made a comment that he's only now having this document placed on the ELMO because he didn't know he would have to challenge these things. That's quite unfounded, even disingenuous, in light of the amalgamated statement the accused has had for quite some time. I think he could easily see that this issue was on the table if he chose to challenge it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Do you confirm that this is -- the Prosecution offered this one-page document to the accused?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: We're now checking the -- this document was just presented to us as soon as the accused made his comment about the provenance we started looking into it. I will advise the Chamber accordingly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. You heard the accused's question, Mr. Gusic, and you have read this passage. Can you confirm that, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You see, before I answer the question I have to point to what the accused said, namely that I had denied something and now he's trying to refute my denying saying that the book is correct and my statement is incorrect. Now, this context that the accused has read out -- if I'm testifying here, do I have right to call him the accused? One would need to read the whole book. I know about this book. I know what it says, and if you read the whole book you get an entirely different impression. Even the accused himself noted that this military staff was established in 1992, and I believe I spoke about that in my previous answers when I said that the Executive Board, sometime in January, February 1992, made a decision to set up this kind of defence staff for Bratunac, because we had certain information that I've spoken to you about the threats to the Bratunac municipality. What this book says is correct, no doubt about it. Samir Nistovic, himself, came like Nurif used to come in 1991. I can't remember the month, September or October, perhaps, 1991, speaking again about those big plans that Serbia and the JNA had concerning the division of Bosnia and the possibility that Bosnia would be attacked and they asked that people organise themselves. And then something was set up it was called I believe the Initiative Board of the Patriotic League, but all that was only done on paper. Nothing really happened in practice. Concerning Nedzib Husic, you can also find more about him in the book. That man stayed in that position for seven or ten days only, and then he realised it was an impossible thing to do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: So do you know the author and title of it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know it's called "The truth about Bratunac." The author is a history professor, Nijaz Masic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Karadzic, please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This says that the SDA in Bratunac set up the Patriotic League in 1991 and its military structure in 1992.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be MFI'd? We'll get hold of the entire book if it's indeed the truth about Bratunac, then we would be interested too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. It will be marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1657, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, please don't hold it against me that sometimes I call you "Witness." Witnesses come one after another. I don't always remember their names.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I've lived through a lot. I'm beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Pobudje a village in Bratunac? Give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know its population?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly. Perhaps a hundred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see 1D4083 in e-court. It's a list of members of the Territorial Defence of Pobudje of April 1992, 434 men, almost all of them from Pobudje, one from Sebjocina who was just visiting or a refugee. Look at page one and then we can look at the last page, the Crisis Staff of Pobudje. You'll see that in April 1991 they were already there, very few joined in June or later. So it's not true what you said a moment ago that you were taken by surprise. Pobudje, a small village, has a battalion of 500. Just as the JNA reported on the plans of the SDA that every municipality should have a 500-strong battalion. Here we see one village has that many.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: What kind of list is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: What is this list? Where has it been taken out of? What kind of document is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: This is Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Territorial Defence of BH, TO Pobudje, list of members of Pobudje Territorial Defence, a document obviously seized in a raid. You see what it says. Crisis Staff. Every name is verifiable, including dates of birth and dates of joining, and most of them joined in April.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I see July 1992. Is it in July that somebody made this list?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Avdo Omerovic made the list in July.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: That's a fair question that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you show the first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: And we can have some information about the provenance of the document rather than sort of an assumption or some kind of projected conclusion. There must be some information about where this document comes from and how the Defence got ahold of it and what it purports to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Let us see the first page, in particular the heading. Can you zoom in a bit further. Can you read the first part, the heading part, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't make it out. It's illegible, but I'd like to state following if I may: This list was made by Avdo Omerovic in July 1992. That means from April to July 1992, the whole Bratunac municipality, apart from this Pobudje village and Konjevic Polje was ethnically cleansed and Muslims were purged out. This village Pobudje and a few other villages such as Konjevic Polje, when they saw what happened in Bratunac and the surrounding villages managed to organise themselves somehow and put up some resistance in that part of the Bratunac municipality. And I allow the possibility that they made this list and some records of their own, but I want to emphasise that this date stated here, the 4th of April that they joined the Territorial Defence on that day, I don't think that's correct. I'm absolutely sure, in fact, it's not correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, did you -- did you say that this document was written or prepared by Omerovic, Avdo?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what it says further down in the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Why don't you show the last page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right. It's not a list of fighting men of Avdo Omerovic. This was signed by the Crisis Staff of Pobudje. So there are more. And looking at page 1, this is part of a collection. It is Annex 17A. It's probably part of a collection belonging to some state authority of Republika Srpska for collection of evidence, and this was seized, as far as I know, in a police raid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: English translation seems to read: "This list does not include fighters in Pobudje from Kamenica led by Avdo Omerovic." Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really don't know, but I suppose that -- you see, what I think this is about these are fighters that managed to organise themselves after Bratunac was occupied. These are places such as Kamenica here are not in Bratunac municipality at all. They're in Zvornik municipality. That was the enclave that was surrounded at the time. So I really can't comment or say anything about this list. All I know with certainty is that on 4th of April, 1992, they did not have any unit at all, because I toured Bratunac municipality at the time, and what I saw with my own eyes was complete lack of readiness in terms of any defence capability.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Please continue, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't see any basis to admit this.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we see 1D4084.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is Brezovica close to you?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: How did you answer the question, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I don't know about Brezovica. Is it a hamlet? Is it a small village? I don't think it's in Bratunac municipality. It doesn't sound familiar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does Avdic, Fahrudin sound familiar?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I know Fahrudin Avdic, but he's from Srebrenica, I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Are these Serbian villages that were attacked by this company from Brezovica? Did this Brezovica company attack villages in Bratunac?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Which Brezovica?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Well, you claim that this whole enclave up to Kamenica and Srebrenica, as you call it the free territory, you say it was united, did Srebrenica units, for instance, attack Kravica on Christmas 1993?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I was not in that territory controlled by the BH Army, but I have some knowledge and some information. There was certain combat involving both sides, attacks by the BH Army and attacks by the VRS. I have information that there was fighting. As far as Kravica is concerned, Kravica was discussed in the Naser Oric trial, and I believe the Defence proved in that case that it was paramilitary operation, and I don't think Naser Oric was convicted on the charges relating to Kravica.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Then we won't deal with this any more, because we can't get an answer, especially not a short one. Mr. Gusic -- can we see 1D4087. Mr. Gusic, is it true that the president of the municipality got a job immediately after his appointment and the chief of the police station also took up his job immediately?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: You mean after they were elected?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'll put it to you this way: Muslims were put into their positions immediately and the Serb commander of the police station was not able to assume his position for a whole year. That's one of the reasons for the tensions.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't recall that the commander of the police station took up his job immediately, but I can't remember why.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Is this the disposition of positions: President of the municipality, secretary of the secretariat for the economy and social affairs, secretary of the Secretariat for National Defence, member of the Executive Board, commander of the TO staff, and there is no commander of the police station listed here, but it's clear that the SDA got that position.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: As far as the police station is concerned, we had certain problems after that ambush in Kravica that happened in 1991. I believe the whole personnel of this police station was replaced, including chief and commander. There were certainly problems.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: You were not the ones who had a problem. Serbs had a problem. Is this the way power was distributed? We can't see the positions of the chief and the commander.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't know about the misdemeanour charge.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The SDS got the position of President of the Executive Board, director of the municipal administration for taxes, director of the municipal administration for surveys, vice-president of the Municipal Assembly, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: As far as I can see, the SDS got six positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: But all of them insignificant. Isn't that right, Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I would not say that they're insignificant. Your president of the SDS for Bratunac, Miroslav Deronjic, was a very skilful politician. You know that much better than I do. And I think that the Serbs were most pleased with this distribution, and they accepted that. We were not pleased. We had 52 per cent. That was the outcome of the elections and that's how power was supposed to be shared. The SDS had 40 per cent and the other parties had 8 per cent. So this was at our detriment -- to our detriment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can this be admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D1658, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we now have 65 ter 742. Page 8 now. Actually, page 7 so that we see the date. Actually, 6. 00835914 is the ERN number. We want to establish that that is a session of the Serb Municipal Assembly of Bratunac held on the 13th of February, 1992. Is that what is written here? Mr. Gusic, does it say the 13th of February, 1992?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Yes. That's what is written here, but I didn't know that you were asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have page 3 now in Serbian. The ERN number 16. That's the last two digits, 16. Down here on the left-hand side it says that item 5 on the agenda was discussed. Mr. Miroslav Deronjic elaborated on this item on the agenda, that is to say the appointment of the commander of the public security station. He said that they intentionally --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we on the correct page? I found that item on page 3 in English, but I don't know where in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In Serbian -- let's move to the left-hand page for the moment and then we'll go back to this that is being displayed right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you see it, Mr. Gusic, towards the bottom? Mr. Miroslav Deronjic elaborated on this item, which is the appointment of the commander of the station, and that is a post that belonged to the Serbs, and he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Probably next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah, Mr. President. It's page 5 of the English, which is the -- ends with the ERN 0613.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read it out you see what it says here: "Mr. Miroslav Deronjic explained this item of the agenda appointing the commander of the SJB. He said that they were intentionally postponing the appointment of the police commander and propose that had we too do not appoint any of their personnel to positions until the issue of ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let's move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You have to make sure the witness it following. Move to the next page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. It's the top of the page: "... until this issue of ours is resolved, appointing the commander that is. Mr. Deronjic's decision was adopted unanimously." Do you see that for all one year the Serbs didn't manage to appoint their personnel in such a sensitive segment, a segment as sensitive as security is?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Let us try to distinguish.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Let us not distinguish anything. Was he appointed or was he not appointed?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: That is no way to talk. You shall speaking about the date of the 13th of February, and you're talking about the Serb Municipal Assembly. That is an illegal entity that was created, I think, in the beginning of January 1992. That is an illegal entity.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I'll answer your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: At that time it was the joint police station; is that not the case?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Please, please. Let us just clarify certain matters for the sake of the Trial Chamber, for the sake of the public. I kindly ask you do have some patience. I'm patient. I'm hearing you out and I'm following all of this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... you were asked about the reason why the certain position in the police was not appointed. Whether that Serbian Assembly was a legal or illegal entity, that's a separate issue. So could you answer the question first and if necessary the accused, the Prosecution or the Chamber will take up the question -- the rest of the question if necessary.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, just two sentences. At the legal Assembly of the Municipality of Bratunac, when power was shared all the positions were filled, the chief of police, the commander, members of the Executive Board from the SDS, at the SDA and so on and so forth. I tried to explain all of that, however, I was being interrupted all the time. There were certain problems in September 1991. In Kravica there was an ambush and two Bosniaks were killed and two Bosniaks were wounded. Since the situation was very tense, inter-ethnic tensions were on the rise. We had interventions from the republican leadership. Mr. Ganic and Mr. Koljevic came, members of the Presidency, both of them. And then the deputy minister of police, Vitomir Zepinic is his name, I think. He's a Serb, with his counsellors, Avdo Hebib, Saric and some other men. At the time they were replaced and then the chief and the commander of the police resigned. Somebody from Tuzla was appointed either chief or commander of the police, someone from the public security there, and for a couple of months he held that position. That was from September 1991 until, say, the end of 1991 or beginning of 1992. So it is not correct what the accused is saying, that for a year and more than a year the Muslim side obstructed this, the appointment of the commander of police. I allow for the possibility there may have been some obstruction from January 1992 onwards when this illegal Serbian Assembly, this illegal entity was founded so perhaps there were some misunderstandings then and some confrontations. Perhaps for some similar reasons our side no longer agreed to appoint the chief of police or, rather, the commander of the police did not have agree to have him appointed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation].

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From September 1991 until the beginning of the war, was it not Muslims who held both positions of commander and of chief of the station?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: September 1991 did you say?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The crisis in Kravica.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I really don't know. I think one person was appointed from the public security stations -- public security centre in Tuzla, and the task was to overcome the problems there and to have an alleviation of the situation there and later on the commander was appointed.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this page be admitted?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: It's already been admitted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that this is part of exhibit that has already been admitted. If you could give the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P3199, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we briefly have D381 to see what Mr. Zepinic and I were saying on the telephone on the 10th of February, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It is Karadzic and Zepinic who is deputy minister who are the interlocutors. Look what Karadzic says here: "Ah-ha Vito, please, now we are suffering the consequences of not having appointed a Serb as milicija commander in Bratunac. Over there they're establishing a borderline in the direction of Serbia and setting barricades and access or, rather, barrier?" Can we have the next page in Serbian. You see what Zepinic says here: "We adopted this kind of decision that pro -- that proposed decision on personnel changes have been cancelled in all stations from heads to deputy commanders." And Karadzic says: "Please, we are going to have to create our police there." And Zepinic says: "Our problem is Bratunac. Our problem is Srebrenica. Our problem is Jajce. The Croats are disputing something and the Muslims won't give them something in Western Herzegovina, that is to say, the Croats both make concessions to Muslims in Western Herzegovina. We are not giving Muslims and we are even now." Karadzic says, "Where are they setting barricades?" And then further down they are saying that they're setting up barriers and they're not letting Serbs enter from Serbia and they are obstructing the freedom of movement. Did you know about all of that?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: First of all, it's not correct. There were no barricades. Secondly, as for someone not letting the Serbs enter Bratunac from Serbia, that's not correct either. I don't know if you remember that sometime then, the end of 1991 or beginning of 1992, Serbia passed a decision on not allowing goods to be exported. Muslims were adversely affected by that. It was the policemen of the MUP of Serbia who were --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Gusic, Serbia did not allow the export of wheat to Bosnia. We ate five times more wheat, but actually we were smuggling it across the border to Serbia. So do not confuse the matter.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: It wasn't only wheat. It was all goods.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: We are going to prove that it's wheat and other strategic materials, and we Bosnians made five times more money on that and Serbia remained without any wheat because of us. Let us look at 3086. That's the 65 ter number. Let's see what happened in Kravica. 30186. This is a conversation between Mr. Zvonko Bajagic and myself. It's on the 4th of September, 1991. Look at the second half: Bajagic is asking whether I know about what is going on, what has been going on since Friday, and I say that I know they shot at the president of the executive council and then this fellow was arrested and then released. And he says yes and then Karadzic says then Muslims were headed to Kravica village. Was their intention to attack or what? Zvonko says no, and I said but, and then Zvonko provides an explanation. Now can we have the next page. There were tensions, there was unrest, and the SUP sent the police to Kravica. It was only Serbs that went there, and in other places there were joint patrols. And then further down: It says after this initial shooting at the president of the Executive Council and Karadzic says all right. That means that I had heard about it. It doesn't mean that it was all right that he was shot. And then Bajagic says: They were wounded and what they did up there in Han Pijesak, that was the pretext. They had already sent information to that effect. And then I say: These two men were wounded. And Bajagic says: After that wounding, again there was an attempted assassination of the president of the Executive Council. And Karadzic says: It was a Serb who was being shot at again. And Bajagic says: Look, you should know what is going on. Let us leave aside this president of the Executive Council. You know that they tried to kill him. And I say: But this president is a Serb, isn't he? And he says: Yes. And then Karadzic says: And these people from Han Pijesak are Serbs who are wounded. And Karadzic says: All right. And then can we have the next page? Last night these four persons took a car and they were moving through Kravica. This is their main military strategist from the SDA and he was a provocateur, and he was in a car with three other men, and he says, yes, yes, they passed through Kravica twice. And Karadzic says, And Kravica is a Serb village. And he says: Yes, Kravica is a Serb village, as a region, and so on and so forth. And then further down: They passed there twice. They went to Konjevic Polje and Konjevic Polje is Muslim. And Karadzic says: So it was a kind of provocation. And he says: Yes. They were going with all the car windows open and with the barrels of their automatic weapons sticking out of these windows. And then they say there are police patrols there. They didn't want to stop. And towards the end, it says, at the exit from Kravica in the direction of Bratunac, Serbs are holding that border. Serbs have their own guards there. Can we have the next page, please. Please read it for yourself. Anybody can read it. And now they're saying somebody from the MUP will come by helicopter and Bajagic says they killed two Muslims. They did not kill the man number one. And then towards the end people from Kravica holding the position. They're not letting a single MUP policeman to get through into their territory. Next page, please. And then he says people from Kravica are very firm. They're not budging. The Muslim police want to come there. Karadzic asks: Are they armed? Bajagic says: Yes, they are. And Karadzic asks: Has anyone had any contact with the volunteers, with Han Pijesak, with the barracks? And you know at Han Pijesak there was a barracks; right?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Karadzic says: No, nobody had any contact about that. Then Bajagic says: At any rate, you should know this is a most urgent matter. Somebody should show up there immediately. There will be trouble big time. Karadzic says: Who? And he says: Somebody from the SDA and the SDS. Karadzic says: To do what? Bajagic says: Well, only the army could go there. They don't trust the MUP. Can we see the next page. And now in the lower third, let me skip this first part, I say: I didn't know that. I only know those two men had died, were killed. I didn't know if it was a provocation or an attack on Kravica. I was with Izetbegovic until ten minutes ago when we were waiting to get real information. Zepinic and Hebib are somewhere up there and Zepinic has not called me yet. He should call me so I can tell him not to send MUP to Serbian villages. Can we see the next page?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Page 6 in English.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note: The last two pages from which the accused has been reading have not been displayed.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And Karadzic says: In your view, who is to blame? And he says: They are to blame. Did not want to stop for two police patrols. They keep their guns out of the window. They were shouting and provoking. Now, let me not read all of this. Karadzic says: And why did that man shoot at the president of the Executive Board? It's probably the next page in English. He got orders. He wanted to assassinate him. Karadzic says: It must have been on orders. They want to fight against the Serbs, and then some profanity. And then he says: In my lay opinion, the SDA leadership must be behind this, because there can't be any better municipality than Bratunac to provoke the Serbs. Bajagic says: If they sacrifice their own Muslim people down there for the sake of a provocation, and then the families are all mixed there. He speaks of Serbs across the Drina. They are bound by bonds of friendship and family bonds. People will not -- people will not wait for official orders to come from Serbia to defend their brothers. And the Muslims will use that. And Karadzic says: Don't let Serbs from Serbia do that and tell those Muslims that they are being sacrificed and that they should not fall for it, because they should not fight us. They can't even threaten us anywhere. Then Bajagic says: Rajko knows what people, Serbs from Kravica or like. They're crazy. I told them, people did you contact the head office? Did you make contact with the SDS head office? Bajagic says: Nobody reacts. I came on my own initiative to inform you. And then Karadzic --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic, you spent ten minutes reading this intercept without putting a question at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: The question is: Mr. Gusic, can you see from this that I had no clue what the local Serbs and local Muslims were doing, that I'm just making inquiries and the head office is not having any control over this?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Can I just ask who this Bajagic is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Don't overlap. Yes. You asked the accused who this Bajagic -- Mr. Bajagic was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Bajagic is a member of the SDS from Vlasenica. He was observing the situation. He asked, "Did you report this to the SDS?" They did not, and he came to inform me.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Just tell me one more thing. At what President of the Executive Board did they shoot?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: From the next passage we see that we don't even know what his name is. Djuka. And then it turns out it Rodoljub Djukanovic. It says an official from the party. Then it says Vlado Djukanovic in the next intercept.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Now I can answer the question. As far as the President of the Executive Board is concerned, Rodoljub Djukanovic, the President of the Executive Board in Bratunac, I can say with full certainty that nobody ever shot at him. Investigation showed later that those men who perpetrated the assassination, Marko Markovic from Ljubovija in Serbia, Radenko Milanovic, also known as Mali Raso, were involved and there were indication that -- indications that some Serb policemen were also involved. So your allegation is, to say the least, not consistent with the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted -- or MFI'd, rather?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We have no basis -- but not through this witness. I was told that this has been already marked for identification. Mr. Karadzic, your time is up but given the situation that it's impracticable to start the next witness, I will give you the rest of the day minus the time for the Prosecution's re-examination. How much would you need, Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I have no re-examination at this point, Mr. President. Can I say one thing about the intercept quickly. We've addressed the issue of admissibility versus MFI. I have no intention of revisiting that even when the accused introduces intercepts by saying let's look at what I was talking about with so-and-so, but given the protocol he should refrain from making -- interjecting commentary in the midst of reading what the intercept contains to explain what he was saying as he did on this occasion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Karadzic, you should take that into account.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would like to make myself clearer, that's -- that's why, and to gain time, but it seems I'm wasting time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see 1D4088, please. Mr. Gusic, please look at this. State Documentation Centre of Republika Srpska. It's a list of war criminals known to the command of the 1st Light Infantry Brigade who committed war crimes in the area of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Milici, Vlasenica and Skelani municipalities and are believed to be in the Srebrenica area. Please look at how many men from Bratunac feature on this list. Seventy per cent are from Bratunac, or 50 per cent, but number 15 is you.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: We see in the heading about this list. "List of war criminals known to the command, et cetera, et cetera, who committed war crimes in the area of Bratunac, Srebrenica, Milici, Vlasenica and Skelani municipalities and are believed to be in Srebrenica." From 17 April 1992 onward, I was not in Srebrenica until the end of the war. I first went back there in 1997 or 1998. So I can say that this list is completely false, not only as far as it concerns me, but many other people listed here who have nothing to do with war crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we see the last page I want to show you out of the total of 387 that 129 are from Bratunac. It says there are indications that you are in Srebrenica; it doesn't say you are certainly in Srebrenica. The document does not challenge the rest.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: The document makes a lot of allegations. The printed media published this entire list and I know a lot of these people on the list never held a gun, had left Bosnia and Herzegovina long before, and they still feature on that list. That's what I'm saying, that all of this should be analysed and verified. A check should be run if it's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: There will be Defence witnesses coming here, too, so we'll do it through them. Can this list be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: No. There's no basis, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I agree, Mr. Tieger. There's no basis on which we can admit this through this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. 1D4089, please. Is this true, what we see written here, Mr. Gusic? Tell the Chamber what it is, because the interpretation is lagging -- or, rather, we don't have the translation yet.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Let me see what this is. I need a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Yeah. There's no translation for this document again, Mr. President, and trying contextually just to figure out what it might be is extremely difficult, so I would ask for the provenance of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Can you help us, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a collection of facsimiles and telegrams that the Defence managed to obtain, and it's material from the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Does it say here that the SDA throughout this period worked continuously both in terms of organised authorities, militarily and politically? Dzevad Gusic as president has been with the fighting men from day one and even was commander of a company.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: If I have to say something about this document, I believe the information listed here is correct. I was a member of the ABH in this period under the command of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina. I can state exactly where I was, in what locations, occupying which positions if you give me time, and I don't see anything in dispute here. All I see is that this is a correspondence between somebody in a small place Bljeceva, and somebody from our own people in Bratunac. Which year is it? Let me see.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: It says -- it says January 1994, and it says that you are deputy commander as of 26 March 1993, and later commander -- assistant commander for moral guidance?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: That's true. I was deputy assistant commander for moral guidance in Kladanj. Kladanj has nothing to do with this. It's a fact. It's easy to prove. I don't know why you insist so much on this document. This is a simple correspondence between those people up there who were in an encirclement and us who were trying to organise themselves.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can this be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Still I'm not satisfied with its provenance, particularly given that it does not reflect the correct diacritics, but in the meantime given the answers given by the witness, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D1659, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I need to tender at least two more documents. One will be very brief showing that this gentleman doesn't know about our interrelations within the SDS. It's 65 ter 603, page 13 out of 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the point of presenting the document if the witness doesn't know anything about it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I want to prove he knows nothing. What he said is totally inaccurate. This document shows that Deronjic and I were very distant. We had a very cool relationship, and we were even political opponents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: You will have another --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just respected the man because he was chosen locally. I directly challenge what this gentleman said. But let us at least have a look at one international document. Can we then see 1D4092, and after that I will say something about the possibility given me to present my defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Just a second. Just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes. Just one, that -- that document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Yes. We have the first page now. This is a member of the European Parliament, Christine Oddy. She is writing to Mr. Petrovski to the Yugoslavian War Crimes Tribunal. Bratunac, Srebrenica, Skelani zone. Then we're going to skip something and then we're going to move on to 0974831. That's the ERN number. It seems to be page 6 in e-court. Yes. Do you see that it is impossible -- I have to read this out to you. "[In English][Previous translation continues] ... We also mention that Serbs have not yet been expelled from the two municipal centres of Bratunac and Skelani, both of which are located on banks of Drina River. Out of the total number of 11.500 Serbs in the Bratunac municipality, only 5.391 or 47 per cent are still there." Do you know, Mr. Gusic, of a single Serb village that remained under Muslim control that had not been burned?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: You see, all of this fighting that you are referring to occurred after I left on the 17th of April when you basically exterminated all the Muslims from Bratunac and --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: These are platitudes, sir, and then you'll have to stay here for a week.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: It's not platitudes. Then there was a certain organisation, and then people were organised in the enclaves and there was active combat on both sides. You know that as well as I do. There was active combat on both sides, you know that as well as I do. In this active combat, there were victims on all sides. There's nothing controversial or unclear there. Of course, I assume -- I mean, I do not doubt that Serb villages fell victim as well as Serb soldiers, Serb civilians. There's nothing for me to challenge there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Can we have -- can we have page 37. In this rush, this is what I'm going to put to you, sir: You evacuated the Muslims --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: What's the relevance of this? Why is it -- it is not a tu quoque.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's not tu quoque. I am proving that that is not what happened, that the Serbs had not attacked. It was the Serbs who were attacked. Three thousand five hundred Serbs were killed in that area, not Muslims. All of this is a lie, Mr. President. All of it is a lie. This is a combatant of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina is speaking here, and he has been marked as a war criminal on this list, and I am challenging everything he said, and I have documents to prove that, and I have no way to defend myself. I have no opportunity to defend myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your last question, Mr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Do you know, Mr. Gusic, that in that area tens of mass graves were found and that General Morillon took part in discovering that and almost all Serb soldiers were killed in Muslim villages and the other way round? Just tell us that. Do you know that in Serb villages a vast majority of soldiers got killed and the other way around?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: I don't really know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: If that is the case, you should explain this to me as a soldier?

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: You should find somebody else to answer all these questions.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have to tell the Trial Chamber that this is no defence and that there is no way of going on this way. I have to look into the matter and see which steps I should take. This is no way to defend oneself. Bringing in a political propagandist of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina to air propaganda here that is presented as evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MORRISON
utterances.text: Dr. Karadzic, it's for the Trial Chamber to assess witnesses. Cross-examination is not the same thing as putting your defence in minute detail. Cross-examination is a discrete art whereby you put the main points with which you disagree with the thrust of the witness's evidence. You are, with respect, actively confusing cross-examination with presenting a defence case. There is an overlap, but they are not the same things.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Regarding the document, Mr. President or just why I was up?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I saw -- you rose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: I think my comments have been pre-empted by His Honour's comments. I was responding to what I considered an inappropriate attack on the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just add something. On page 865, in the chapter entitled "Organisers of the Crime," this member of the European Parliament came to the information that this witness is in place five or six, the fifth or sixth person on the list, and if that is not relevant to you and if that does not impeach this witness, I really do not see how someone can defend oneself.

utterances.speaker: DZEVAD GUSIC
utterances.text: Well, you show me this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: I have the number. Let's see this 0974865.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But is this part -- is this part of the same document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Your answer, Mr. Gusic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No comment. This is something -- I don't want to say anything that would be bad manners in any way, although the accused would deserve that. What he said over the past ten minutes or so are pure fabrications and nothing else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Tieger, as to the admissibility of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Well, I -- it seems to me at a minimum -- well, let me address this issue. There -- the accused is trying to present this document as if it's an investigation of the international community. It's patently the provision by this particular member of the international community of documents presented to her by Serbian authorities and a simple look at page 37, which was displayed by the accused, illustrates that. The language of that document -- that page of the document is very clear that it was drafted by Bosnian Serb officials. I was going to say at a minimum I invoke a comment by -- and an observation by Mr. Robinson the other day and that is certainly nothing more could be considered for admission than the particular pages displayed to the witness of this voluminous document, but beyond that, the Court needs to be aware, I think, that the suggestion that this was somehow independently compiled by the international community rather than being a transmission of materials submitted to it by Bosnian Serb authorities needs to be considered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Given the time, we'll give the ruling as to its admissibility tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: And we'll hear any submission, if any, tomorrow, but we need to conclude today.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just indicate that it is impermissible to leave aside what a member of the European Parliament did a long time ago in 1993. We can disregard a member of the European Parliament and cannot do that to a member of the Bosnian Army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: That's a separate matter whether to admit this document through this witness. In any event, Mr. Gusic, your evidence has been concluded and on behalf of this Chamber I'd like to thank you for coming to The Hague to give it. Have a safe journey back home. Tomorrow --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to thank you as well, very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: We'll continue tomorrow at 2.15. And I'd like to thank the indulgence of the staff members. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Thursday, the 25th day of August, 2011, at 2.15 p.m.
